title: Deuxieme Sonatine
identity: Charles Koechlin, Deuxième Sonatine, Op. 194 no. 2 (composed 1942–43). IMSLP identifies a soprano saxophone-or-oboe d’amore solo with piano, and a separate ensemble version. The opened score scan is the ensemble version. A publisher catalogue lead describes an alto-or-tenor edition, so the assigned soprano instrument tag needs edition verification.

evidence.claim: Schott/Max Eschig identifies the edition as op. 194/2 for oboe d’amore or soprano saxophone and piano, with intermediate label and 18 pages.
Retailer identifies four movements, 34 pages for the broader score listing, and full original ensemble scoring.
A conservatory syllabus lists the soprano saxophone version among its repertoire options.
evidence.source_name: Conservatorio Superior de Música de Navarra syllabus

evidence.claim: Arno Bornkamp recording listing gives the four movement names and durations.

IMSLP record identifies Op. 194, composed 1942–43, with a two-player oboe d’amore (or soprano saxophone) and piano version, and a distinct ensemble version. The accessed score PDF is the ensemble scoring, not the piano version.
A separate saxophone-catalogue search result lists Sonatine No. 2, Op. 194 for alto or tenor saxophone and piano, conflicting with the soprano version in the score’s title page.

score_observations.claim: The opened 28-page ensemble edition title page labels the solo instrument oboe d’amore or soprano saxophone. Opening line begins Andante, très calme, presque adagio at pp=, with a slurred chromatic line, very soft dynamic, and changing meters; p. 2 continues with chromatic motion and triplets over sustained ensemble parts. This is not the piano-reduction edition.
score_observations.source_name: IMSLP-EU scan of the ensemble edition, pp. 1–2

review_focus: Inference from the ensemble score: inspect chromatic fluency, sustained soft control, meter changes, and coordination with the independent ensemble parts. The piano reduction and its saxophone part were not inspected.
collection_flag: Original work with alternate oboe d’amore/soprano saxophone scoring; separate piano and ensemble versions. Edition and saxophone type require confirmation.

listening.description: Arno Bornkamp, soprano saxophone, with Ivo Janssen, piano; four movements listed.
listening.verification: Album listing checked; playback not auditioned.

score_links.description: Ensemble-scored edition with soprano saxophone or oboe d’amore solo; opening pages inspected. Not the piano reduction.

gaps: The inspected notation is the ensemble edition, not the assigned piano reduction.
Resolve soprano versus alto/tenor instrumentation among edition listings.
No matching saxophone recording or specific college use verified.
